text: Gl $PENG longs
🚢 it?

Taiwan monthly sales data for $8299.TW is out, another strong month with 301% YoY revenue growth. Is it cyclical? Who knows. Bears will never be satisfied in this spot and will continue telling you that quality compounders are risk free in a world of impending artificial superintelligence.

In "Are you a memory man - Part 2" (link in QT) i talked about $8299.TW as a possible beneficiary of a major industry goal to move KV Cache / Context to NAND instead of $DRAM, given it is about 100x as cheap. Since then, a lot of developments have become chalk - Kioxia is directly working with $NVDA on a solution using StorageNext, there's rumours of $SKHY and $8299.TW working with $NVDA on a solution using a phison controller, etc. We even saw @ID_AA_Carmack weighing in on the theme (call back from my VR dev days!).

It still remains to be seen how much of an economic impact this will have on Phisons earnings (the future they are building for has not arrived yet), but it seems like they are making all the right moves - preparing the end markets by selling high density SSDs, building out their capabilities with AIDAPTIV+ R&D, etc.

Overall it was a fine week for the portfolio. NAV remained roughly stable (although down small today), but a solid bounce and a trim in $GTLB left us a bit better positioned across factors etc. Biotech has mostly performed quite well and a nice diversifier.

Today was a rare day where I didn't make a few of medium sized trades. It feels like we have stopped oscillating between software is dead and semiconductors are dead and biotech is dead and hyperscalers are dead, and most sectors seem somewhat rationally priced. $CRM is a little cheap in my mind, but not enough to go overweight. $AVGO is probably a little cheap, but i am already quite long MediaTek which i prefer. I still like $SPGI but up 14% from where I bought it and after the  Global Mobility spinoff, not worth going overweight. Same with $CAI, $TEM, $CELC, etc. I like them all, even at these levels, but not enough to go overweight.

$VEON seems the cheapest to me still here, and so i have ramped that, but at ~10% of net, not really anywhere to go from here either. Korean small cap seems very undervalued still, but I am long enough on that trade i think.

Marketplace platforms like $SE, $MELI etc have caught up and now seem more rationally priced.

On the short side it has been very difficult to find things to short that are correlated with longs. In semiconductors $ALAB and $ARM are the two that seem most out of whack, but i closed out $ALAB for an L and am waiting to take another crack at that. Probably after doing some more study on their Scorpio Smart Fabric Switches. $LSCC seems potentially overvalued, but i think to short that one you need a pretty deep view of the tech. Quite a lot of work to put a .5% short on. I have learned not to do it simply on valuation here.

Unfortunately on $ARM I am already short very bigly (largely covered by $9984 long as well as big CPU positions in $AMD and $INTC that are somewhat correlated).0

$AAPL seems potentially shortable here for funding. They have been absolutely crushing it, but I think one thing AI has shown is that it is a quality killer - if the thesis is an unbreakable moat at 40+ PE, i think the last year has introduced tail risk. I would always say things like 'no one is ever going to wear $META glasses over $AAPL ones'. But with the OpenAI Codex super app actually starting to feel kind of... incredible... and an unlimited budget for a hardware team.... and Jony Ive... I mean, I don't think the hardware is going to dethrone Apple, but a new paradigm seems to be taking shape. There are more players than ever before, more risk. $NVDA desktop pcs for the home... OpenAI pendants... $META glasses.... On top of that, a massive memory shortage leading to price hikes. China is sold out (see Xiao Mi). Even if Apple gets a deal to buy from there, it is not the end of the shortages. But, need to think about this one more. I would snap buy Apple shares at 22 PE, so, not sure a short is justifiable. But maybe.

In terms of research i'm looking at, I have started ramping up my studies of Alzheimers when I have time. I am still looking for an entrance on $QTRX and hope to be fully there on alzheimers by then (they make a diagnostic for it).

I'd also like to buy another defense name or two. I bought a little $KRKNF on the dip, seemed ok. With the upcoming Anduril IPO, i think its a reasonable place to spend some brain cycles. The Heavy Names in Japan look credible too ($7011 / $7012).  Might also consider re-entering $NXSN if it gets cheap enough. Fingers crossed there, great company.

$PENG was going great until today but i resisted the urge to sell yesterday- the numbers seem too good for now not to go for the 1 year minimum hold. But that probably puts it right near the top of my 'work more on this company' list.

Well, our attempt to stick the landing looks like it might have gotten waylaid by a little greed last week. Although I’ve generally had a plan of rebalancing toward less heavy sector weightings (sticking the landing if you will). But after seeing some deals across the compute space i closed out a $DRAM hedge and added to some other compute adjacent names, mostly Siemens Energy and $FLNC. That said, nothing too crazy. Adjusted net exposure has floated up to 89.8% which is just a hair above our general 85% target, and sector diversification has been pretty solid.

This market can quickly punish this sort of thing though - the day after closing out the memory hedge, the Iran war immediately resumed and fear built to a cacophony on X, with Chinese models and memory bearposting being the main FUD’s of the week. Fear largely seems driven by vocal investors cashing out to lock in gains to me. The chinese models cost just as much to serve as the US ones, which means that we are just going to have an even bigger compute shortage. And though the idea that OpenAIs model is getting open sourced 3 months after release, I think most people who aren’t using this tech underestimate the difficulty to serve it. That said, in the short term, it does feel like momentum has turned. What these investors are going to invest in, I don’t know - a lot of people across the AI trade seem to only want to invest in momo stocks because for them, stocks are like sports teams - their whole online identity is wrapped around the securities they own. To me it feels like they will just cash out, pay a bunch of tax, and then buy higher ‘when the market is more favourable’ which seems silly. Those that hold with a long term view or diversify across some other sectors seem wiser to me.

With that in mind, i am eating my own cooking, and in terms of good things, I am pretty diversified across sectors. Healthcare alone is 25% of adjusted net exposure, with $PSNL driving gains and a new large position in $XGN, a small cap autoimmune diagnostics business. Interestingly, $CELC sold off after hitting their PDUFA. I added a hair there at around $89. We will see if that is prudent or not.

On the financials side, $SPGI has performed beautifully. I only wish I had bought more. Results oriented, but mostly because it would diversify us well. I kept with a normal position size, but as such, I am still less heavily weighted to non-AI names than i would hope. That said, the large $DAVE position has done well, and i trimmed some long term lots (still big). $7974 has also continued to trade as ‘inverse-memory’, which is nice.

I have also built some decent sized positions in Software and Aerospace and Defense (most recently the Korean names), which have added some more diversification across the book, but again, a little too small if the mentality was to end up less exposed to the AI trade. Importantly on the software side, I completely cut $GTLB here - I almost got even after averaging down continuously. Ideally I would have trimmed to a more normal position size, but I couldn't take the remaining 11% ST loss if i did that, so i sold the whole position and will revisit later. I do think the spot is good but there is slightly more risk - OpenAI and Anthropic are both definitely building solutions internally. I think $IBM remains a credible buyer however, and organic growth is still quite good as they move toward metered billing for some spend.

We shall see how the coming week goes but my base view is there is going to be continued selling across the compute trade, but that i will aim to ride it out. As i mentioned to a friend, if you are worried about being long Kioxia here, your position is just too big. The PE and growth is about as good as you get investing. There is some risk, but there is always some risk. Just don't be all in.
